sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球供应链制造母港、跨境电商货源地与外资合规准入市场

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Blank-Check Entity for Public Market Acquisition Mergers (SPAC)

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Taiwan (province of China; independent company registry and tax administration under the Cross-Strait legal framework)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Continental/Statutory Law) supplemented by administrative regulations; the Cross-Strait Act (Act Governing Relations between the People of the Taiwan Area and the Mainland Area) applies to mainland Chinese shareholders
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Cross-Strait Economic Cooperation Framework Agreement (ECFA), signed 2010
Cross-Strait Bilateral Investment Protection and Promotion Agreement, signed August 9, 2012
Cross-Strait Agreement on Avoidance of Double Taxation and Strengthening Tax Cooperation, signed 2015 (signed but not yet in force)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Taiwan Money Laundering Control Act (洗錢防制法), as amended; Counter-Terrorism Financing Act (資恐防制法); Company Act (公司法) Articles on shareholder registers and directors; Regulations Governing Money Laundering and Countering Terrorism Financing of Financial Institutions (FSC); MOEA Company & Commerce Registration Directives; and the Cross-Strait Act for mainland investor licensing.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Certificate of Incorporation and Current Business License of the mainland Chinese corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) / local Administration for Market Regulation, PRC
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Mainland notarization followed by SEF/ARATS cross-strait authentication; Taiwan is not a Hague Apostille party)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original shareholders' resolution / board resolution of the mainland investor authorizing the Taiwan SPAC incorporation and equity investment
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors / Shareholders' Meeting of the PRC corporate shareholder (notarized by local PRC notary)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Audited financial statements of the mainland corporate shareholder for the latest fiscal year
Certified copies of passports and PRC resident identity cards of all individual ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public, PRC / issuing authority of the individual documents

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letters and source-of-funds statement for each contributor to the escrow/trust acquisition corpus
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized and authenticated as applicable; accepted by TW financial institutions under KYC/AML internal policy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney appointing the Taiwan-based incorporation agent and applicant

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the Taiwan Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) sanctions lists, OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council consolidated list, and EU/UK consolidated sanctions; enhanced proportionate due diligence on domestic and international politically exposed persons (PEPs) under FATF Recommendation 12 and Taiwan Money Laundering Control Act Article 10; cross-border PEP and mainland Chinese official status screening because the investor is a PRC entity; risk-based EDD required for the SPAC's target acquisition pipeline before any escrow release.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Taiwan Company and Commerce Registration Information System (經濟部商工行政服務入口網 / gcis.nat.gov.tw); Company Name and Business Scope Pre-examination Online Application (公司名稱及業務預查線上申請)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered legal name must be in traditional Chinese characters; simplified Chinese or Romanized transliterations are not accepted for the statutory name; one English name may be recorded as an alias but does not form the legal name. The mandatory suffix for a stock-issuing vehicle is 股份有限公司 (Company Limited by Shares). The proposed name must be distinguishable from all existing registered names, reserved names, and trade names of the same or analogous business categories.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: 銀行 (Bank) — requires prior FSC approval
保險 (Insurance) — requires prior FSC approval
證券 (Securities) — requires prior FSC approval
期貨 (Futures) — requires prior FSC approval
金融 (Financial) — requires prior FSC approval
信託 (Trust) — requires prior FSC approval
政府 (Government) / 國立 (National) / 總理 / 總統 — deemed misleading and prohibited
特殊目的收購(SPAC) — triggers FSC anti-evasion review; cannot be used unless the vehicle obtains the necessary securities/business license
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The pre-examination approval is valid for 180 days and may be extended once for a further 180 days by filing a maintenance application before expiry. If the name is rejected, the applicant may either (i) re-file a new pre-examination application after amending the name or business scope, or (ii) file an administrative appeal (訴願) with the Ministry of Economic Affairs within 30 days of receipt of the rejection notice under the Administrative Appeal Act, followed by administrative litigation before the Taipei High Administrative Court if the appeal is dismissed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices (商務中心) are tolerated by the MOEA for maintenance of a registered address, provided the address is a physical commercial location in Taiwan which accepts legal service and tax correspondence. However, for a SPAC/blank-check vehicle in ISIC 6499, the FSC and commercial banks will require substantive local presence—physical office lease, local directors, board minutes in Taiwan, and local books—so reliance on a bare virtual office is not prudently permissible for licence and escrow-banking purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 35% within the first 12 months given the blank-check/financial vehicle designation; rising to greater than 50% if any FSC approval or stock-exchange listing is pursued; baseline 15% for a purely private shell with no licensed activity.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: MOEA statutory tariff: TWD 300 per application

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Company Act registration tariff: TWD 1,000 standard filing fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Mainland investor investment permit application (陸資投資許可申請)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: IO fee schedule for cross-strait investment applications: approximately TWD 10,000

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization, SEF authentication and translation of PRC corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: PRC notary publics and Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing notarial and SEF authentication tariffs (per document)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: FSC business license / regulatory authorization fee for blank-check financial vehicle
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: FSC application fee schedule for securities/financial vehicles: approximately TWD 100,000

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Physical registered office lease (12 months, part-time commercial centre)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Private commercial landlord / registration service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing Taipei/Taoyuan market rate for registered office with receiving service

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company seal set (company chop, bank chop, small seal) and statutory records books
Incorporation and regulatory legal counsel (pre-incorporation due diligence, UBO filing, license drafting)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed-fee engagement at prevailing market benchmark for cross-strait SPAC incorporation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT internal control program, PEP screening software and annual compliance officer retainer
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Taiwan law/accounting firm and screening vendor
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for medium-risk financial vehicle (first-year retainer)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act, including Articles 4, 18, 129-156, 192-217, and 356-1 onward where applicable to public companies; Foreign Investment Act for non-Taiwanese investment approval; Securities and Exchange Act and Financial Supervisory Commission and Taiwan Stock Exchange rules governing public offerings, listing, securities firms, and SPAC transactions. Taiwan has no statutory Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture form; the entity should generally be incorporated as a company limited by shares or company limited by shares with foreign investment.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce, or the competent municipal or county government company-registration authority, depending on the registered office location; foreign-investment matters are administered through the Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Name and Business Scope Reservation Application, Articles of Incorporation, and Company Registration Application (公司登記申請書), together with the Foreign Investment Approval Application where applicable.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Taiwan generally imposes no universal statutory minimum paid-in capital for an ordinary company limited by shares, but capital must be sufficient for the proposed business and must be fully subscribed and paid before registration. Capital verification by a Taiwan certified public accountant is required. Foreign-invested capital must be remitted through an approved inward-remittance process and recorded in the company's designated account. A SPAC or listed vehicle remains subject to FSC, TWSE, broker-sponsor, underwriting, escrow, and minimum financial requirements that may exceed ordinary incorporation requirements. The approximate electronic company-registration fee is NT$700; paper filing, name reservation, certification, translation, CPA, investment approval, and securities-market fees are additional.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Resolved that the Company accepts the subscriptions for its issued shares as set out in the approved subscription schedule and confirms that all subscribed capital shall be paid into the Company’s designated bank account and verified in accordance with Taiwan law. Resolved further that the registered office at [full Taiwan address] is adopted with effect from incorporation. The Board appoints [name] as Chairperson, [name] as General Manager, [name] as Company Secretary or designated statutory filing officer, and authorizes the Chairperson to complete company registration, foreign-investment filings, banking arrangements, tax registration, and all ancillary governmental submissions, subject to applicable FSC and TWSE approvals.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm Legal Form, Name, and Permitted Business Scope
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce company-name and business-scope search system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Replace the non-statutory Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture designation with an available Taiwan company form. Reserve the Chinese company name and business activities. Use the correct securities, investment, and holding-company business codes and do not describe the vehicle as a bank, fund, broker, or asset manager unless separately licensed. Obtain documentary evidence of the registered office and confirm that the proposed activities are compatible with FSC and TWSE rules.
required_dossiers: Proposed Chinese and English company names
Proposed business scope and industry codes
Registered-office lease, consent, or ownership evidence
Foreign investor corporate certificates and constitutional documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Amend the proposed name or business codes and resubmit. If the authority identifies a regulated activity, obtain written confirmation or preliminary approval from the FSC or the relevant sector regulator before filing incorporation documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Foreign Investment Approval and Complete Capital Remittance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs; designated Taiwan bank for inward remittance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the foreign-investment approval application before capital remittance where required. Submit legalized or certified foreign shareholder documents, ownership information, ultimate beneficial ownership information, investment plan, funding source, and proposed Articles. After approval, remit the subscription funds into the designated Taiwan account using the approved investment route. Obtain bank remittance evidence and arrange CPA capital verification.
required_dossiers: Foreign shareholder certificate of incorporation and good-standing or equivalent document
Foreign shareholder board or shareholder investment authorization
Passport or identity documents of directors and shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to information requests through the filing agent or authorized representative, correct ownership or source-of-funds inconsistencies, and submit supplemental legalized documents. Do not treat capital as paid until the remittance and verification requirements are satisfied.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute Incorporation Documents and Appoint Corporate Officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company shareholders, board of directors, Taiwan notary where notarization is required, and designated company-registration authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Finalize and sign the Articles, shareholder subscription schedule, consent to director appointments, director and supervisor or audit-committee arrangements, registered-office consent, and first board resolution. Taiwan notarization is not universally required for every company document, but foreign-executed documents generally require notarization or certification, apostille or consular legalization as applicable, and certified Chinese translation. Ensure statutory director eligibility and conflict disclosures.
required_dossiers: Shareholder meeting minutes or incorporation consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure defective signatures, missing certifications, translation discrepancies, or incomplete director consents. Re-execute and re-notarize documents where the registry rejects formal defects.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Company Registration and Tax Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs or competent local company-registration office; National Taxation Bureau of the Ministry of Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Company Registration Application with the Articles, capital verification, foreign-investment approval, shareholder and director information, registered-office evidence, and fee payment. After issuance of the company registration certificate and unified business number, complete tax registration, accounting-book setup, invoice registration, and beneficial-owner and anti-money-laundering records. Open the permanent corporate bank account and transfer verified capital as appropriate.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Answer registry queries within the stated cure period, replace non-compliant forms, correct business-scope language, and resubmit through the online or paper channel. An appeal or administrative review may be considered for a final adverse decision, subject to applicable procedural deadlines.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Securities, SPAC, and Listing-Related Regulatory Approvals
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Supervisory Commission, Securities and Futures Bureau; Taiwan Stock Exchange; Taipei Exchange where applicable; Taiwan Securities Association and the appointed securities firm or sponsor
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before conducting any public offering, listing, underwriting, securities dealing, investment management, or acquisition activity requiring approval, obtain the applicable FSC authorization and engage an eligible securities-firm sponsor or underwriter. Prepare the prospectus, governance framework, escrow or trust arrangements, investor-protection disclosures, acquisition timeline, redemption mechanics, related-party controls, AML procedures, and listing application. Do not market shares publicly or accept public subscriptions before the relevant approval and prospectus requirements are satisfied.
required_dossiers: TWSE or Taipei Exchange listing application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Address FSC, exchange, sponsor, or underwriter comments through a formal deficiency-response package. Amend the prospectus, governance documents, escrow terms, or business scope and resubmit. Any public-offering or listing activity must remain suspended until written approval is obtained.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Financial Supervisory Commission, Securities and Futures Bureau, with Taiwan Stock Exchange or Taipei Exchange as the relevant market operator. The Ministry of Economic Affairs is the corporate-registration authority but is not the primary securities regulator.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: FSC approval for the relevant public offering, securities-market activity, or regulated financial business, together with TWSE or Taipei Exchange listing approval for a SPAC. Incorporation alone does not authorize securities underwriting, brokerage, investment management, public solicitation, or listing.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment, Taiwan, and the competent local environmental protection bureau
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Generally exempt from project-level EIA and industrial environmental permits where the SPAC conducts only office-based corporate, financing, and securities activities without manufacturing, construction, land development, material storage, wastewater discharge, or air-emission sources. A full EIA or other environmental approval may become mandatory if the project includes a physical facility or a listed development category under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: For a normal office-only SPAC, no industrial wastewater, VOC, or process-emission threshold is ordinarily triggered. The company must still comply with applicable waste sorting, general waste disposal, sewage, building, and hazardous-material rules. Any facility generating wastewater, air pollutants, VOCs, hazardous waste, or regulated chemicals must obtain the relevant discharge, air-pollution, waste, and chemical-management permits before operation and meet Taiwan's applicable effluent, emission, monitoring, storage, and licensed-disposal standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: An office-only SPAC normally requires no manufacturing-site operating clearance, but the registered premises must satisfy building-use, occupancy, fire-prevention, emergency-exit, and electrical-safety requirements. Obtain confirmation from the competent local fire department where required by building classification, occupancy change, floor area, or fit-out works. Structural-load approval is required for alterations, heavy equipment, or changes affecting the building structure. Workplace compliance includes Labor Occupational Safety and Health Act requirements, emergency procedures, employee safety training, and any applicable labor-insurance and health-examination obligations. Manufacturing, warehousing, or laboratory premises require additional fire, structural, occupational, hazardous-material, and local-government approvals.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Taiwan Ministry of Finance (MOF), administered operationally by the relevant National Taxation Bureau (NTB) and its local branch office. Corporate registration is generally coordinated through the Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) one-stop company registration system. Tax and business tax services are available through the MOF eTax platform and the relevant NTB electronic filing systems.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Sino-foreign equity joint venture established in Taiwan must first complete company incorporation or foreign-invested company registration with the MOEA or the competent local authority, obtain approval for foreign investment where applicable from the Department of Investment Promotion under the MOEA, establish its registered office and bank arrangements, and apply for business tax registration with the competent NTB before commencing taxable business activities. The NTB issues an eight-digit Unified Business Number (UBN), which functions as the entity's principal tax identification and business tax registration number. The application normally requires the company approval or registration documents, articles of incorporation, responsible person's identification, registered office evidence, capital and shareholder information, foreign-investment approval documents where applicable, business premises documentation, and a power of attorney for an agent where used. A foreign company conducting business through a Taiwan branch follows the branch-registration and business-tax-registration process and receives a Taiwan tax identification number. Separate registration may be required for withholding tax, customs importer/exporter status, payroll obligations, electronic invoices, and regulated securities or financial activities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Taiwan does not provide a United States-style check-the-box election for a Taiwan company or equity joint venture. A Taiwan company is generally subject to Taiwan profit-seeking enterprise income tax at entity level, with dividends potentially subject to separate shareholder-level taxation or withholding. A branch is taxed on Taiwan-source profits under branch rules and generally does not constitute a separate legal person. There is no general statutory hybrid-mismatch election that converts a Taiwan limited company into a transparent partnership for Taiwan tax purposes. Available statutory choices are limited and fact-dependent, including qualifying income-tax incentives, approved tax holidays, industry-specific investment incentives, foreign tax credit claims subject to statutory limits, head-office expense allocation methods for branches, and, where legally available, profit-seeking enterprise income tax filing methods. A SPAC, acquisition vehicle, or investment company does not obtain pass-through treatment merely because it is formed for a special purpose. Conducting securities, investment advisory, trust, escrow, payment, or other regulated financial activities may require separate approval from the Financial Supervisory Commission or another competent authority and may affect the applicable tax and reporting profile.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Taiwan Value-Added Tax (VAT), administered under the Value-Added and Non-Value-Added Business Tax Act. Taiwan generally uses a credit-invoice VAT system for ordinary taxable businesses. Customs duties and import VAT are separately administered at importation by the Customs Administration under the Ministry of Finance.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Business tax registration is generally required before commencing business operations and is not subject to a general annual turnover threshold for ordinary businesses. Certain small businesses and specified exempt or special-category businesses may be assessed under separate rules; a commonly applied small-business threshold is monthly sales of approximately NT$200,000 for qualification for small-business assessment treatment, but that threshold does not create a general exemption from all registration, invoicing, or tax obligations. A Taiwan JV carrying on taxable business, including taxable services, investment-related services, or other commercial activities, should register irrespective of expected turnover unless a specific statutory exemption applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan electronic invoices are issued under MOF electronic-invoice regulations through an approved electronic-invoice platform, the MOF e-Invoice Platform, or an approved software and certificate arrangement. Electronic invoices must contain the prescribed seller, purchaser, transaction, tax, invoice-number, and authentication data and must be transmitted to the MOF platform or otherwise reported through the prescribed electronic channel within the applicable statutory period, commonly within two days after issuance for business-to-business electronic invoices, subject to transaction-specific rules and approved arrangements. Taiwan does not generally operate a universal pre-issuance real-time VAT clearance model equivalent to jurisdictions requiring invoice-by-invoice government approval before delivery. Digital signatures, approved certificates, electronic invoice formats, buyer-consent or system requirements, cancellation and allowance documentation, and retention controls apply. Businesses must retain invoice records and supporting books for the statutory period, generally at least five years, and must reconcile electronic invoices with VAT returns, customs declarations, accounting records, and payment evidence.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated VAT may generally apply to goods exported from Taiwan, goods sold to export-related businesses in qualifying transactions, and services supplied to foreign customers or used outside Taiwan where the statutory conditions and documentary evidence requirements are satisfied. For exported goods, the taxpayer must establish that the goods physically left Taiwan and that the export transaction corresponds to the VAT invoice and accounting records. For services, the taxpayer must establish the foreign customer's identity, the contractual scope, the place and beneficiary of actual use, payment evidence, and that the service qualifies as an offshore or other statutorily zero-rated service rather than a service performed or consumed in Taiwan. Zero rating is not automatic for a foreign-currency transaction, an offshore contract, an investment transaction, or a payment received from a non-Taiwan account. Input VAT refunds may be claimed by qualifying businesses, including exporters, but require reconciliation of input invoices, customs records, output transactions, and payment documentation. A SPAC acquisition, listing, underwriting, advisory, trust, escrow, or securities transaction should be separately analyzed because many financial services may be exempt rather than zero-rated, and exempt activity can restrict input VAT recovery.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Taiwan Customs export declaration or electronic export declaration showing the exporter, consignee, goods description, value, tariff classification, and customs release or export confirmation
Commercial invoice and packing list matched to the export declaration
Bill of lading, air waybill, or other carrier transport document evidencing shipment from Taiwan
Sales contract, purchase order, service agreement, or other transaction document identifying the foreign customer and commercial purpose
Proof of delivery or carrier export confirmation where required by the NTB
Foreign-exchange receipt evidence, bank credit advice, remittance record, or other acceptable proof of collection where required for the relevant transaction
VAT sales invoice, zero-rated invoice, credit note, and electronic invoice transmission records

For qualifying offshore services, evidence of the foreign customer's status, service performance location, service-use location, deliverables, correspondence, personnel or system logs, and confirmation that the service was not used in Taiwan
Accounting ledger, accounts receivable reconciliation, bank statements, and VAT return schedules linking the transaction to the zero-rated claim

Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent bank evidence where specifically required by the bank, tax authority, or transaction type; Taiwan law does not make one uniform certificate mandatory for every export transaction
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Taiwan does not impose one universal 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for every export or offshore-service transaction. The 180-day field is retained as an internal compliance control and must be validated against the transaction type, Central Bank foreign-exchange rules, banking documentation, contract terms, and any applicable investment or export-control requirements. The NTB may deny or revoke zero-rating where export movement, offshore use, customer identity, payment, invoice, or service-location evidence is incomplete or inconsistent. Denied zero rating may be reassessed as taxable at the applicable VAT rate, with recovery of improperly refunded input VAT, interest, and applicable penalties. Failure to issue, retain, report, or correctly transmit invoices may result in administrative fines and repeated-violation sanctions under the Value-Added and Non-Value-Added Business Tax Act and related regulations. False declarations, fabricated customs or bank documents, concealed sales, circular payments, or fraudulent refund claims may trigger tax evasion penalties, criminal liability, customs penalties, disgorgement, and assessments covering prior audit periods subject to statutory limitation rules. The taxpayer should preserve a transaction-level audit file and obtain advance written guidance from the competent NTB for material or novel offshore-service and financial-transaction classifications.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The payload identifies both China (CN) as the sovereign country and Taiwan (TW) as the jurisdiction, while describing a Sino-foreign equity joint venture. These identifiers do not establish a single applicable banking or foreign-exchange regime. For a mainland China-incorporated entity, the principal authorities are the People's Bank of China (PBOC) and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE). For a Taiwan-incorporated entity, the relevant monetary authority is the Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) (CBC); mainland China rules should not be applied to it. Confirm the place of incorporation, registered office, and account location before opening accounts or executing transfers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Mainland China generally permits current-account foreign-exchange transactions, including bona fide trade payments and qualifying profit remittances, subject to bank review, authenticity checks, tax evidence, and applicable SAFE requirements. Capital-account transactions remain regulated; foreign-invested capital contributions, cross-border loans, equity transfers, and capital repatriations must follow applicable registration, account-use, and transaction-documentation rules. A dividend remittance typically requires distributable profits under audited financial statements, completion of loss and reserve allocations as applicable, tax compliance evidence, and bank review. No assumption should be made that a SPAC's fundraising proceeds, acquisition funding, or securities-related receipts qualify as ordinary trade flows. Taiwan operates under a separate foreign-exchange framework; its rules must be assessed independently if the entity or account is in Taiwan.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For mainland China, there is generally no universal statutory requirement to convert all export proceeds into renminbi or to surrender them at a fixed conversion ratio. Export proceeds remain subject to applicable foreign-exchange administration, bank authenticity and consistency checks, trade-document verification, and current reporting or monitoring requirements. Receipt timing and permitted account treatment depend on the transaction, the company's registration status, and current SAFE and bank rules; confirm the applicable rules with the handling bank before shipment and collection. This statement does not determine Taiwan export-proceeds requirements.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited (ICBC)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account, subject to the applicable mainland China foreign-investment registration and bank approval
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account, subject to the applicable mainland China foreign-investment registration and bank approval
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account, subject to the applicable mainland China foreign-investment registration and bank approval
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account, subject to the applicable mainland China foreign-investment registration and bank approval
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account, subject to the applicable mainland China foreign-investment registration and bank approval

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a substitute for a licensed domestic bank account for mainland China capital contributions, regulated capital-account transactions, or RMB settlement. An offshore electronic money institution may support limited payments only where the relevant service, counterparty, currency, and transaction are legally permitted. It does not replace mainland China bank, SAFE, foreign-investment registration, or capital-account requirements. If Taiwan is the actual jurisdiction, assess the provider under Taiwan law and its local licensing and cross-border payment rules.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no single statutory rule requiring every director to appear physically for every account opening. The account-opening bank determines whether in-person attendance, a local legal representative, wet-ink documents, notarization, or an interview is required. Remote or representative-assisted onboarding may be available in some cases but must not be assumed, particularly for a foreign-invested entity, a complex ownership chain, a SPAC-related business, or accounts receiving cross-border capital. Confirm requirements with the selected branch before execution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the stated mainland China entity and the Taiwan jurisdiction identifier, or uncertainty over the place of incorporation, tax residence, and account location.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the current business license or equivalent incorporation evidence, constitutional documents, registered-address evidence, tax-registration details, ownership chart, and written confirmation identifying the governing jurisdiction and intended account location. Resolve the CN/TW mapping before submitting the application.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SPAC or blank-check acquisition activity, securities fundraising, or an asserted business scope requiring a statutory license or regulatory approval.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a precise business description, regulatory-perimeter analysis, all applicable licenses and approvals or a reasoned explanation of why none are required, offering and listing documents where applicable, acquisition mandate, target and investor screening procedures, and a transaction-level source-and-use-of-funds schedule. Do not characterize securities or acquisition proceeds as trade receipts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial ownership, nominee arrangements, politically exposed persons, sanctions exposure, or high-risk investor and target jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a fully traced ownership chart through natural-person ultimate beneficial owners, identification and address evidence, control and voting-rights analysis, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds records, sanctions and PEP screening results, and supporting corporate records for each intermediate entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border capital contribution, shareholder loan, acquisition funding, or remittance inconsistent with registered capital, declared purpose, or account classification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide executed subscription or investment documents, shareholder resolutions, applicable foreign-investment and SAFE or bank registration records, capital-account or loan documentation, remitter and beneficiary details, board-approved funds flow, and evidence that the amount and purpose are consistent with the relevant registration and account mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dividend, service-fee, interest, or other outbound payment lacking a clear legal basis, tax treatment, or commercial substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide audited financial statements, distributable-profit and reserve calculations where relevant, board or shareholder approval, contracts and invoices for non-dividend payments, tax filings and withholding evidence, transfer-pricing support where applicable, and bank-required remittance documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected use of client money, subscription proceeds, or acquisition escrow without clear ownership, segregation, or release conditions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the trust or escrow agreement, beneficial-ownership and control terms, permitted-use restrictions, subscription and redemption mechanics, release conditions, independent trustee or custodian details, investor disclosures, and applicable regulatory approvals. Confirm that the chosen bank offers the required account type.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For a mainland China entity, obtain the required foreign-investment, capital, or cross-border financing registration and open the appropriate bank account before remittance. Instruct the remitter to use the exact registered legal name, account details, currency, and transaction purpose; provide the subscription or investment agreement, shareholder resolution, remitter identity, ownership information, and registration evidence requested by the handling bank. The bank must verify the transaction and applicable account-use rules before credit or conversion. Do not use a trade-purpose code for equity, loan, securities, or acquisition funding. Purpose-code selection and reporting are bank- and transaction-specific; obtain written confirmation from the handling bank rather than inventing a code. If the intended jurisdiction is Taiwan, use its separate registration and reporting procedures.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For bona fide mainland China trade payments, use a bank-authorized cross-border remittance, commonly SWIFT MT103, supported by the underlying contract, invoice, transport or customs evidence where applicable, and beneficiary details. A commercial letter of credit may be used where commercially appropriate and issued subject to the bank's credit approval and applicable rules. For acquisition, securities, shareholder, or capital-account payments, use the legally applicable capital or investment route and supporting approvals and registrations; do not route them as trade settlements. For any escrow, confirm permitted account use, segregation, release conditions, and bank acceptance before funds are sent. Taiwan transactions require a separate local-rule assessment.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with an eligible bank, subject to applicable mainland China rules, genuine underlying exposure or other permitted basis, documentation, and bank suitability requirements.

Non-deliverable forwards only where the relevant bank, currency pair, counterparty, transaction purpose, and applicable cross-border rules permit the product; confirm settlement and reporting treatment before execution.
Foreign-exchange swaps with an eligible bank where permitted and supported by an appropriate exposure, liquidity need, and transaction documentation.

Do not treat this list as approval for speculative trading, unregistered capital transactions, or hedging by an entity that lacks the required eligibility; Taiwan-based activity must be assessed under Taiwan rules.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Business Report, audited Financial Statements, and Earnings Distribution Plan approved at the Annual General Meeting (Company Act Articles 20, 21, 228, 230)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) Company Registration Office via the e-Company Registration Portal or the district Commercial Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM must convene within 6 months of fiscal year-end (June 30 for calendar-year entities); MOEA filing due within 15 days after AGM approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Responsible person fined NT$10,000–NT$50,000 (approx. USD 315–1,560) per violation; repeated non-filing permits MOEA administrative strike-off and dissolution order under Company Act Article 10

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return (Form 45) with schedules and loss carry-forward reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau (NTB), Ministry of Finance, district office of the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: May 1 – May 31 immediately following the close of each taxable year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing: 1% surcharge every 2 days up to 10% of assessed tax (Tax Collection Act Article 20); evaded tax penalty up to 3x plus asset seizure and departure ban on the responsible person

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Business Value-Added Tax (VAT) return for each two-month period, including reconciliation of SPAC escrow or trust account interest
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the 15th day of each odd-numbered month (Jan 15, Mar 15, May 15, Jul 15, Sep 15, Nov 15) covering the preceding two-month period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative late-filing fine NT$1,200–NT$12,000 (approx. USD 35–375); concealed VAT subject to 3%–5% supplementary tax; overdue beyond 30 days triggers tax liquidation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Register of Members, Register of Beneficial Owners (UBO Register), and share-transfer filings submitted as annual attestation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: MOEA Company Registration Office / Central Business Registration Data System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation incorporated with the Annual Business Report by June 30; any share transfer or UBO change filed within 15 days of the transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: False or omitted UBO records: fine NT$50,000–NT$500,000 (approx. USD 1,550–15,600) under Company Act Article 22-1 and Money Laundering Control Act; criminal referral for forged attestation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Mainland-China-invested enterprise annual operational declaration for mainland shareholders in the Taiwan JV, with updated SPAC equity structure
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: MOEA Investment Commission (Cross-Strait Investment Approval Unit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by May 31 for the preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine NT$60,000–NT$2,500,000 (approx. USD 1,875–78,125) under the Act Governing Relations between the People of the Taiwan Area and the Mainland Area; revocation of mainland investment permission and forced divestiture in serious cases

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report (Shareholders' Meeting Report Book) and audited statements published on the Market Observation Post System (MOPS) for the public-registration SPAC vehicle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC), Securities and Futures Bureau
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual report delivered within 30 days after the AGM (in all cases by July 31); audited annual statements filed with FSC by May 15
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine NT$240,000–NT$4,800,000 (approx. USD 7,500–150,000) under Securities and Exchange Act Article 178; blank-check registration and listing approval may be revoked

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual AML/CFT compliance self-assessment, risk-rating results of the SPAC trust account, and compliance officer certification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: FSC Anti-Money Laundering Division (Banking Bureau / Securities and Futures Bureau)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after fiscal year-end (March 31 for calendar-year entities) for designated business types under Money Laundering Control Act Article 5
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine NT$200,000–NT$10,000,000 (approx. USD 6,200–312,500) and forced replacement of the AML compliance officer; persistent non-compliance grounds license suspension or revocation

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent CPA audit and attestation where paid-in capital is NT$30 million (approx. USD 940,000) or above per Company Act Article 20 and MOEA Order; any FSC-registered public issuer or SPAC; total annual revenue exceeding NT$100 million; or when shareholders holding 10% or more request a special audit under Company Act Article 245.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: FSC-registered SPAC and public issuer level: Taiwan IFRS as endorsed by the FSC; non-public JV holding company: Taiwan Enterprise Accounting Standards (EAS / 企業會計準則公報); both frameworks require compliance with the Business Entity Accounting Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Taiwan does not use a generic annual return form; non-public companies must maintain a paper Register of Members and Register of Beneficial Owners at the registered office, disclose any mainland or foreign shareholder holding 10% or more, identity the underlying natural-person beneficial owners, and file every change with MOEA within 15 calendar days. Annual confirmation is completed by uploading the UBO sheet with the Annual Business Report to MOEA by June 30 and by obtaining formal shareholder attestation of the share register at the AGM; all share transfers settled during the year must be entered in the register before the attestation is minuted.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 480 – 1,200 per annum (Taipei registered-office and corporate secretarial services; excludes filing fees and audit costs)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,500 – 12,000 per annum for a non-operating SPAC holding entity under EAS-based CPA audit; FSC-public issuers requiring consolidated IFRS audited statements typically range from USD 18,000 – 40,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 20% corporate income tax on Taiwan-source taxable income. An additional 5% tax generally applies to undistributed current-year earnings retained after the statutory distribution period.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Taiwan generally provides a 20% corporate income tax rate. Eligible enterprises may claim investment tax credits, research and development credits, accelerated depreciation, and industry-specific incentives under applicable statutes, including the Statute for Industrial Innovation. Tax holidays are not generally available merely because the entity is a foreign-invested joint venture or SPAC vehicle. The alternative minimum tax regime may apply to qualifying entities and income items. Dividend distributions to nonresident shareholders generally attract withholding tax at 21%, subject to applicable relief.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return, generally filed through the Ministry of Finance electronic filing system for profit-seeking enterprises. The competent tax authority is the National Taxation Bureau having jurisdiction over the company's registered office. Supporting financial statements, tax reconciliation schedules, related-party disclosures, and transfer-pricing documentation must be retained and produced upon request.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; a provisional income tax return is generally required for the first six months of the fiscal year unless an applicable statutory exemption or approved alternative applies.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year company, the annual corporate income tax return is generally due from 1 May through 31 May of the following year. A provisional return for the first six months is generally due during 1 September through 30 September. A company using a non-calendar fiscal year generally files within the prescribed period following the end of the relevant fiscal year. Tax payable is generally due by the applicable filing deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Unified Business Number, legal name, registered address, accounting period, industry classification, legal representative, paid-in capital, and filing status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Taiwan-incorporated joint venture is a Taiwan resident company and must report its own Unified Business Number and Taiwan registration details. A nonresident shareholder is not entered as the taxpayer unless it independently files Taiwan-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest income, investment income, foreign-exchange gains, service income, gains or losses on securities or investments, and other income recognized under Taiwan tax rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report Taiwan-source income earned by the Taiwan company. Income earned directly by a foreign shareholder or foreign sponsor must not be improperly booked as company income. Cross-border receipts must be classified by legal substance and source.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable operating expenses, payroll, professional fees, financing costs, depreciation, amortization, provisions, transaction expenses, and documented business expenditure.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to nonresidents require review for Taiwan-source characterization, withholding, permanent-establishment exposure, beneficial ownership, deductibility, and supporting contracts. Expenses must satisfy business-purpose, documentation, and arm's-length requirements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit or loss reconciled to taxable income through additions and deductions for non-deductible expenses, exempt income, tax depreciation, impairment, provisions, and statutory adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign accounting standards or group reporting figures cannot replace Taiwan tax reconciliation. Foreign taxes, withholding taxes, and foreign exchange items must be separately analyzed for creditability and deductibility.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses carried forward from prior years, subject to the statutory ten-year period and applicable book, audit, and filing conditions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses of a foreign shareholder, offshore affiliate, or nonresident sponsor cannot be transferred to the Taiwan company absent a specific statutory basis. Changes in ownership and business restructuring require anti-avoidance review.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transactions with related enterprises, including capital contributions, shareholder loans, interest, guarantees, management fees, service fees, royalties, asset transfers, securities transactions, and reimbursements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose and document transactions with the Chinese parent, offshore sponsors, affiliates, directors, trustees, escrow providers, and financing parties. Apply Taiwan transfer-pricing rules and withholding requirements independently.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Taxable income and corporate income tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income multiplied by the applicable 20% rate, after permitted deductions, credits, and loss utilization.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not net shareholder-level withholding taxes against company corporate income tax unless legally available. Tax credits require statutory eligibility and documentary support.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits for provisional tax, withholding tax, advance payments, and other legally recognized payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments made by foreign parties do not automatically constitute Taiwan tax credits. Payment evidence and the legal taxpayer identity must match the Taiwan company's return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculation of the additional 5% tax on undistributed earnings, including permitted exclusions, retained earnings adjustments, and qualifying reinvestment amounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The additional tax is imposed at company level before later shareholder distributions. A SPAC should document escrow restrictions, redemption obligations, transaction costs, and the commercial basis for retained earnings.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign-source income, foreign tax paid, foreign tax credit calculations, and supporting certificates where credit relief is claimed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign tax credit is subject to statutory limitations and documentary requirements. Mainland China and Taiwan do not generally operate a comprehensive income tax treaty equivalent to a bilateral DTA for ordinary corporate distributions; treaty relief must not be assumed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration by the responsible person, electronic submission, financial statement attachment, tax payment confirmation, and retention of accounting records.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The legal representative and authorized tax agent should verify beneficial ownership, related-party disclosures, withholding reconciliations, and consistency with securities, company, AML, and foreign-exchange filings.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing may result in a statutory surcharge generally calculated by reference to tax payable, subject to minimum and maximum amounts; a return with no tax payable may still attract a fixed administrative fine. Failure to pay assessed tax generally attracts a late-payment surcharge calculated under the Tax Collection Act, commonly 1% for each two-day period of delay up to the statutory cap, plus interest or enforcement costs where applicable. Failure to file may permit tax assessment based on available information and may cause loss of loss-carryforward or incentive eligibility. False reporting, concealment, fabricated invoices, or evasion may trigger fines, tax recovery, administrative penalties, and criminal prosecution.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Provisional Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return, filed through the Ministry of Finance electronic filing system where required.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year company, the provisional return for January through June is generally filed from 1 September through 30 September of the same year, with payment by the prescribed deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income and expenses for the first six months, adjusted under Taiwan tax rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use Taiwan-company records and Taiwan tax adjustments; do not substitute group consolidated figures.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax calculated on the provisional taxable base, less legally permitted credits and payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border withholding and foreign taxes require separate legal analysis and cannot be claimed solely on group accounting records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Payment of provisional tax and subsequent credit against annual corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Retain bank evidence, payment references, and reconciliation to the annual return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or inaccurate provisional filing may result in administrative fines, additional assessment, late-payment surcharges, and interest. The annual return remains independently required even if provisional tax was paid.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 21% withholding tax generally applies to dividends distributed by a Taiwan company to a nonresident company or individual. Dividends to Taiwan-resident individual shareholders are generally subject to the domestic imputation and withholding rules applicable to the shareholder. A 5% additional tax may apply to undistributed earnings at company level.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, confirm that the recipient is a treaty resident, beneficial owner, and eligible recipient under the applicable Taiwan income tax agreement. Obtain a current certificate of tax residence issued by the foreign tax authority, verify limitation-on-benefits or anti-abuse requirements where applicable, analyze beneficial ownership and substance, and submit the prescribed application or supporting documents to the competent tax authority when prior approval is required. The payer must withhold at the domestic rate unless treaty relief is properly available and documented. A Chinese mainland shareholder should not receive DTA relief merely by presenting a mainland tax registration certificate because Taiwan and mainland China do not generally provide a comprehensive operative income tax treaty for this purpose.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid by a Taiwan company to a nonresident are generally subject to 20% withholding tax, subject to statutory exemptions, reduced deemed-income rules, or treaty relief. Interest paid to a nonresident is generally subject to 20% withholding tax for many categories, but 15% or other rates may apply to specified loans, securities, government or approved financial instruments, and treaty-qualified recipients. Dividends are generally 21%. The applicable rate depends on payment classification, recipient status, source rules, beneficial ownership, treaty eligibility, and whether the recipient has a Taiwan permanent establishment. Payments to related parties must also satisfy arm's-length and thin-capitalization rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Taiwan transfer-pricing documentation is transaction- and taxpayer-specific. A commonly applied Local File documentation exemption threshold is annual net revenue below NTD 300,000,000 or aggregate annual related-party transaction amounts below NTD 200,000,000, subject to statutory exceptions and transaction categories. A Master File is generally relevant where the Taiwan entity belongs to a multinational enterprise group with consolidated revenue of at least NTD 7,500,000,000 and the applicable related-party conditions are met. Country-by-Country Reporting generally applies at the group level where consolidated revenue reaches NTD 27,000,000,000. Thresholds must be confirmed against the rules applicable to the relevant fiscal year.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Other OECD-consistent methods supported by reliable comparability analysis and Taiwan regulations
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Taiwan does not operate a single standalone economic-substance regime identical to the UAE ESR framework. Substance is nevertheless relevant under Taiwan transfer-pricing, beneficial-ownership, controlled foreign company, general anti-avoidance, withholding-tax, permanent-establishment, business-tax, and company-law principles. A Taiwan SPAC vehicle should maintain genuine governance, directors' decision-making, accounting records, bank and escrow controls, personnel or appropriately documented operational capability, commercial purpose, transaction oversight, and evidence that functions, assets, and risks match reported profits. Pure conduit arrangements, circular funding, nominee directors, artificial interest or royalty flows, and treaty shopping may be recharacterized or denied.
special_purpose_acquisition_company_cont: Document the commercial purpose and legal ownership of sponsor shares, founder shares, warrants, escrowed proceeds, redemption rights, and acquisition-related fees.
Separate investor funds, sponsor funds, operating cash, and escrow assets in accounting and banking records.
Apply arm's-length pricing to sponsor services, underwriting, advisory fees, shareholder loans, guarantees, and post-merger transactions.
Assess whether acquisition activity constitutes securities, investment, trust, financial, or other regulated business requiring approval or licensing.
Reconcile tax returns with Taiwan Stock Exchange, Taipei Exchange, Financial Supervisory Commission, company registry, AML, and foreign-exchange filings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate income tax evasion and false reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing taxable income, fabricating expenses, using false invoices, understating gains on securities or investments, misclassifying shareholder funds, or submitting materially false tax returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of unpaid tax, penalties that may be calculated by reference to the tax evaded, late-payment surcharges, interest, assessment based on available information, and possible criminal prosecution under Taiwan tax laws. Criminal consequences depend on the statute, amount, intent, and evidence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The responsible person, director, manager, accountant, or other participant may face administrative fines, civil restitution, joint liability where legally applicable, disqualification or regulatory action, and criminal imprisonment. Corporate limited liability does not protect intentional personal misconduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlicensed financial, securities, investment, or trust activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a public-market acquisition vehicle, soliciting investments, managing investor assets, operating an escrow or trust arrangement, dealing in securities, or providing investment services without required FSC, securities, trust, banking, or other authorization.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Orders to cease operations, cancellation or suspension of business, disgorgement, administrative fines, investor compensation, transaction invalidation risks, and criminal penalties under the Securities and Exchange Act, Banking Act, Trust Enterprise Act, Company Act, or other applicable laws.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and responsible officers may face criminal imprisonment, fines, civil compensation, removal, regulatory bans, and liability for investor losses. Travel restrictions may be imposed in enforcement or criminal proceedings where statutory conditions are satisfied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML, counter-terrorist financing, and beneficial-ownership failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unidentified investors, concealing ultimate beneficial owners, using nominees, processing unexplained Swift wires, failing to conduct enhanced due diligence, ignoring sanctions indicators, or failing to file suspicious transaction reports.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines, compliance orders, account or transaction restrictions, suspicious-transaction investigation, asset freezing or confiscation, and criminal penalties for money laundering or terrorist financing. Penalties depend on the entity's regulated status and the underlying offense.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, officers, and facilitators may face criminal imprisonment, fines, civil asset recovery, disqualification, and regulatory enforcement. A corporate structure does not shield knowing participation, willful blindness, or obstruction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abuse of escrow, investor funds, or redemption proceeds
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Commingling escrowed subscription proceeds with operating funds, unauthorized withdrawals, related-party transfers, circular funding, false redemption records, or use of investor money for sponsor expenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Restitution, disgorgement, civil damages, regulatory sanctions, fines, suspension or revocation of approvals, and potential criminal prosecution for breach of trust, fraud, embezzlement, or securities violations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may be personally liable for restitution and investor losses and may face criminal imprisonment, fines, asset seizure, director disqualification, and restrictions on leaving Taiwan during proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Inflated advisory or management fees, non-arm's-length shareholder loans, excessive interest, artificial royalties, unsupported guarantees, cost allocations without benefit, or shifting SPAC profits to the Chinese parent or offshore affiliates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax adjustment to arm's-length income, denial of deductions, additional tax, withholding-tax assessment, penalties, interest, transfer-pricing documentation penalties, and possible general anti-avoidance action.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and responsible persons may face civil tax liability where statutory conditions apply, fines for false declarations, professional sanctions, and criminal exposure if the arrangement involves intentional evasion, fraud, or forged documentation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Applying reduced treaty rates without residence certificates, paying a conduit entity, misclassifying dividends as interest or royalties, failing to withhold, or asserting mainland China treaty relief that is not legally available.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Withholding-tax assessment against the payer, collection of unpaid tax, interest, penalties, denial of treaty benefits, and potential liability for inaccurate withholding filings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The responsible person and withholding agent may face statutory fines, civil liability for unpaid amounts where applicable, and criminal exposure for deliberate concealment or falsification.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False corporate records and sham capitalization
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Back-to-back capital contributions, fictitious paid-in capital, nominee shareholders, circular loans presented as equity, fabricated board minutes, or undisclosed sponsor control.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Company-law penalties, capital verification challenges, registration cancellation or rectification, tax reassessment, creditor claims, disgorgement, and criminal prosecution for fraud or false statements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, founders, accountants, and responsible persons may incur civil liability to the company, shareholders, and creditors and may face imprisonment, fines, disqualification, and asset recovery.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to maintain books, records, and tax documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to retain accounting records, transfer-pricing files, contracts, bank evidence, escrow reconciliations, beneficial-owner records, invoices, or proof of cross-border services.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines, estimated assessment, denial of deductions or credits, loss of tax incentives or loss carryforwards, audit extension, and adverse evidentiary presumptions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The responsible person and accounting personnel may face fines, professional discipline, civil liability for resulting tax losses, and criminal exposure if records were destroyed or falsified.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Unapproved capital remittances, disguised loans, unauthorized offshore transfers, inaccurate investment registrations, or routing investor funds through accounts inconsistent with approved purposes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Foreign-exchange administrative fines, forced repatriation, transaction cancellation, account restrictions, tax reassessment, and criminal exposure in cases involving fraud, laundering, or prohibited transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may face personal fines, restitution, regulatory sanctions, criminal investigation, asset restraint, and travel restrictions where legally ordered.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Direct or indirect dealings with sanctioned persons, restricted Chinese entities, prohibited technology or defense-related targets, or concealment of the ultimate destination of funds or assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transaction blocking, asset freezing, administrative fines, license denial, forfeiture, criminal prosecution, and loss of market or listing approvals under applicable Taiwan and cross-border laws.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance personnel may face criminal imprisonment, fines, asset confiscation, disqualification, civil claims, and travel restrictions. Ignorance is not a defense where due diligence obligations were breached.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Fraudulent acquisition disclosure or market manipulation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misrepresenting a target, inflating valuation, trading on material nonpublic information, making false public disclosures, coordinating artificial prices, or using sponsor information for undisclosed personal benefit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Securities penalties, disgorgement, investor compensation, trading bans, listing sanctions, administrative fines, and criminal imprisonment for insider trading, market manipulation, fraud, or false disclosure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, sponsors, underwriters, advisers, and officers may be personally liable for investor losses and face imprisonment, fines, disqualification, asset seizure, and travel restrictions.
